Synopsis:
Animal dialogue - a skittish beast of burden.A deep rothe that's being used by some duergar to clear rubble - only it smells death and is unwilling to work. The player can try to calm the beast (through Speak with Animals or Animal Handling) and encourage it to calm down and return to work, or to turn against the duergar. If the player fails to calm the rothe, it will turn on both them and the duergar.

Cluster Contexts:
- UND_FearfulRothe_Rothe_001.json: Off-screen, Herdmaster Skarjall and his duergar crew have been beating and driving a deep rothé and other pack beasts to clear a rubble choke, and Skarjall—winded and cramping—already knows there’s an adamantine forge buried under the stones (he even produces an adamantine scrap and frames the find as clan property). The rothé is skittish, reeking of death from whatever lies under the rubble, and is unwilling to work unless calmed; it will become primed to attack if fear or threat is not relieved. The player can use Speak with Animals or Animal Handling to soothe the beast and either coax it back to obedience or encourage it to turn on the duergar; the provided dialogue variants show both calming and incitement outcomes. If the player fails to calm the rothé, it will likely lash out at both the party and the duergar; Skarjall is predisposed to violence if the forge or beasts are threatened.
- UND_FearfulRothe_Rothe_002.json: Panicky and bestial. A one-liner deep rothe speak with animals dialogue. It's being used by duergar to clear rocks, only it and another rothe have been unsettled by strange noises and stopped responding to their masters. It can be calmed so it can return to its work (the act of calming occurs when speaking to the othe rothe, whom this one takes its cues from).
- UND_FearfulRothe_AD_RotheFrenzy.json: The duergar reacts to some deep rothe (bull-like creatures) turning hostile.
- UND_FearfulRothe_Guard_002.json: One of the duergar guards near some deep rothe that're being used as hauling animals. Gruff and grim. Little patience and less empathy.Different reactions if:- animals are panicking;- animals are calm;- animals are dead (doesn't matter how);
